stories.headline: Fire at girls' school in Kenya kills at least 16 students, injures scores more, government official says
stories.summary: A fire at a girls' secondary school in Kenya's Rift Valley has killed at least 16 students and injured scores more. The blaze occurred overnight in a dormitory at the school, located in a town in central Kenya. Search teams have been deployed to the scene. The cause of the fire is not yet known. This incident is the latest in a series of school fires in Kenya, where many students board due to long commutes. A similar incident in 2024 at Hillside Endarasha Primary in Nyeri county resulted in the deaths of at least 17 students. The government has confirmed the death toll, with many more students injured in the fire. The exact number of injured students is not yet confirmed.

stories.headline: With threat to ‘blow up’ Oman, Trump adds another country to his attack list
stories.summary: US President Trump threatened to "blow up" Oman on Wednesday, amid reports that Muscat is holding talks with Iran about overseeing passage through the Strait of Hormuz. The strategic waterway is a crucial route for international oil trade. Trump's threat against Oman adds to a growing list of countries he has threatened to attack or has actually attacked. The threat comes as tensions between the US and Iran remain high. Oman's talks with Iran about the Strait of Hormuz are seen as an attempt to reduce tensions in the region. Trump's comments have sparked concern and criticism, with some viewing his threat as an escalation of already heightened tensions between the US and Iran. The threat against Oman is the latest in a series of aggressive statements made by Trump against various countries.

stories.headline: Five people have been found trapped in a flooded cave in Laos
stories.summary: Five villagers trapped in a flooded cave in central Laos for over a week have been found alive by rescue divers. The group was discovered sitting on a rock in the darkness, huddled together in a small, muddy chamber. Two other villagers who were with them are still missing. The rescue operation was deemed dangerous, but the discovery of the five alive has brought hope. Rescuers plan to start bringing the group out on Thursday. The villagers were found by divers Mikko Paasi and Norrased Palasing, who filmed the scene, capturing the emotional moment with sobs heard in the background. The rescue efforts are ongoing, with focus on locating the two missing individuals and safely extracting the survivors from the cave.

stories.headline: SA mining sector gatvol with DMPR over endless cadastre delay
stories.summary: The South African mining sector is frustrated with the Department of Minerals and Petroleum Resources (DMPR) over the delayed launch of the mining cadastre system. Initially promised to go live at the end of June 2025, the launch was restricted to the Western Cape as a test drive in May 2025. However, "data issues" caused further delays in February 2026. The lack of a functioning cadastre system has contributed to a significant backlog in mining applications. The new system aims to provide a more predictable and efficient framework for securing and managing mineral rights. Despite the delays, the DMPR's efforts to roll out the system highlight its commitment to digital transformation and regulatory efficiency in the mining industry. The sector is eagerly awaiting the implementation of the cadastre system to address the ongoing backlogs and inefficiencies.

stories.headline: Spotify Podcast Clips Feature Announced for Quick Sharing of Podcast Segments
stories.summary: Spotify has introduced a "Podcast Clips" feature, allowing users to share specific portions of a podcast with others using a link. The feature includes a trimming tool that lets users select the beginning and end of a clip, although it currently uses a transcript-based selector. Saved clips are stored in the user's Spotify Library, enabling them to revisit or add them to playlists. The feature is rolling out globally to free and Premium users on mobile, with availability expanding to more shows over time. Users can create and share short podcast clips directly from the app using a scissors tool, preview clips before sharing, and save them in a "Your Clips" collection or library. Clips can be shared as links, chapters, or timestamps, making podcast discovery more social and accessible. The feature is expected to increase viral moments and help new listeners find shows.

stories.headline: Bungie Is Letting Players Try Marathon for Free for a Limited Time
stories.summary: Bungie is offering a free trial for Marathon from June 2nd to June 9th on Xbox Series X|S, PS5, and PC, coinciding with the launch of Marathon Season 2. During this time, players can try the full game at no cost, and any progress made will carry over to the full game if purchased. This move comes as Bungie shifts focus to Marathon, following the announcement that Destiny 2 will receive its final content update in June. The studio aims to revitalize the extraction shooter with significant changes, attempting to regain players. The free trial period allows potential players to experience the game before committing to a purchase, with all progress retained if they decide to buy the game after the trial.

stories.headline: I tested the Fitbit Air vs Garmin Forerunner 70 Can the $99 Fitbit compete with the $249 Forerunner 70
stories.summary: The Fitbit Air and Garmin Forerunner 70 were compared in a head-to-head test. The $99 Fitbit Air was found to be as competent and reliable as the $249 Garmin Forerunner 70 in measuring heart rate and metrics like speed, pace, and distance during outdoor workouts. In a step count test, both devices were within five steps of the actual tally, a highly accurate outcome. The significant price difference between the two devices may prompt Garmin to reconsider their pricing strategy, potentially delaying the launch of their upcoming CIRQA model to address areas where Fitbit outperforms them. The Fitbit Air's performance has raised questions about the value proposition of the more expensive Garmin Forerunner 70, with the Fitbit Air selling for $99.99, significantly less than the Garmin's estimated $199-$249 price point.

stories.headline: TechLife Pad Plus 2 Price in the Philippines, Specs & Features The TechLife Pad Plus 2 is now official in the Philippines with a 12-inch 2K display, MediaTek Helio G100 processor, 9000mAh battery, and LTE connectivity
stories.summary: The TechLife Pad Plus 2 tablet is now available in the Philippines, featuring a 12-inch 2K display, MediaTek Helio G100 processor, and 9000mAh battery with LTE connectivity. The device has 8GB of RAM, expandable up to 12GB, and 128GB of storage, expandable up to 1TB. It also comes with an 8MP rear camera, 5MP front camera, and quad stereo speakers. The tablet runs on Android 16 and supports 18W charging and 5W reverse charging. Initially offered at an early-bird price of Php 11,699, the suggested retail price is Php 14,999. During the launch period, customers can enjoy up to Php 3,300 off through vouchers and receive a free keyboard when purchasing online through Shopee, Lazada, or TikTok. The tablet is available in three colors: Storm Grey, Moonlight Silver, and Starlight Pink.

stories.headline: Chelsea set £120m asking price for Enzo Fernández - report Strong stance from the club
stories.summary: Chelsea has set a £120m asking price for midfielder Enzo Fernández, who has been linked to Real Madrid. Despite preferring to keep the 25-year-old, the club is open to a sale at the specified price. Fernández, who joined Chelsea in January 2023 for £106.8m, is reportedly seeking Champions League football and is eager to make a move during his prime. His contract with Chelsea runs until 2032, but the club has not made progress in contract negotiations. A sale at the demanded price would represent a significant profit for Chelsea, and the club is likely to hold out for the full amount in any potential transfer deal. Fernández's desire for Champions League football has put pressure on finding a resolution that benefits all parties involved.

stories.headline: Record nine Premier League teams confirmed for European competitions Nine Premier League teams will take part in European competitions next season. This is a joint record for English clubs.
stories.summary: Nine Premier League teams will participate in European competitions next season, matching the all-time record for English clubs. The top five teams in the Premier League qualified for the UEFA Champions League. Additional teams secured spots through other channels, including the FA Cup final. Manchester City's win in the FA Cup final confirmed at least eight Premier League teams would play in European competition next season. The final team secured its spot, bringing the total to a record-tying nine teams. This achievement marks a significant presence of English clubs in European competitions, with the teams set to compete in various tournaments, including the Champions League, next season. The record was confirmed after the final day of the Premier League campaign and recent cup competitions.

stories.headline: Champions League final: Ranking the 10 most iconic individual performances Steven Gerrard in Istanbul? Gareth Bale's double? Teddy Sheringham or Ole Gunnar Solskjaer? Ranking the best Champions League final performances.
stories.summary: The top 10 most iconic individual performances in the Champions League final have been ranked. Steven Gerrard's performance in Istanbul is considered one of the most memorable, along with Gareth Bale's double and the goals of Teddy Sheringham and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer. Other notable performances include those of Lionel Messi and Didier Drogba. The rankings are based on a combination of last-gasp goals, all-round artistry, and outstanding goalkeeping displays. The list is part of a discussion on the official UEFA Champions League Fantasy Football game, where fans can pick their dream team and compete against friends. The rankings are open to debate, allowing fans to have their say and share their own opinions on the most iconic Champions League final performances. The discussion is accompanied by graphics and leaderboards from THE FINALS video game.

stories.headline: GT vs RR Today Match Prediction and Betting Tips, Odds and Live Score Cricket prediction for Gujarat Titans (GT) vs Rajasthan Royals (RR), Indian Premier League, 2026, t20, 19:30 IST 29 May 2026.
stories.summary: Gujarat Titans face Rajasthan Royals in IPL 2026 Qualifier 2 at the Maharaja Yadavindra Singh stadium in New Chandigarh. Rajasthan Royals have a perfect record at this venue this season, winning all three matches. The Royals are coming off a strong performance, with Sooryavanshi scoring 97 off 29 balls against SRH. In contrast, Gujarat Titans were recently defeated by RCB, losing by 92 runs. The head-to-head record and current form suggest a closely contested match, but Rajasthan Royals have an edge, particularly given their unbeaten record at the venue. Chasing teams have won approximately 60% of matches at this stadium, making the toss crucial. With a place in the final at stake, both teams will look to give their best performance. Rajasthan Royals are the favored team to win, with their moneyline being the best bet.

stories.headline: Rajasthan woman, 22, pregnant with sixth child for another son; doctor raises alarm
stories.summary: A 22-year-old woman in Rajasthan is pregnant with her sixth child, reportedly because her family wants another son. The woman, already a mother of five, has drawn attention to the risks of early marriage and maternal health. Local health officials have raised concerns about the situation, highlighting the need for better health awareness and family planning in rural areas. The incident has sparked discussions on the importance of addressing early motherhood and the desire for male children in some communities. Authorities are likely to intervene to provide medical care and counseling to the woman, while also addressing the underlying social issues contributing to such situations. The case has gone viral, prompting a wider conversation about women's health and family planning in India.

stories.headline: Indian man returns home after 20 years in Saudi prison, reunites with mother
stories.summary: Abdul Rahim, an Indian man from Kerala, has returned home after spending 20 years in a Saudi Arabian prison. He was convicted in connection with the death of a 15-year-old Saudi boy with disabilities in 2006, in what was described as an accidental incident. Rahim had initially faced a death sentence but was pardoned and released after serving a 20-year prison term under Saudi law. A global campaign and crowdfunding effort raised Rs 34 crore in blood money to secure his release. Rahim reunited emotionally with his mother in Kozhikode, Kerala, on the occasion of Eid al-Adha, marking a poignant homecoming after two decades. The Indian Embassy confirmed his pardon and release, bringing an end to a long and complex legal battle in Saudi Arabia.

stories.headline: Escaping Saudi death row, man returns to Kerala
stories.summary: Abdul Rahim, a Kerala native, has returned to Kerala after spending 20 years in a Saudi prison. He was sentenced to death for accidentally causing the death of a boy. A massive global crowdfunding campaign was launched to raise "blood money" for his release. The campaign collected around Rs 47 crore, with Rs 34 crore paid as blood money, meeting the deadline of April 18, 2024. This payment paved the way for Rahim's release from death row. He was welcomed by relatives and well-wishers in Kozhikode upon his return on May 28. The crowdfunding effort was supported by people from various walks of life, including daily wage laborers, who contributed to save Rahim's life. His release marks the end of a nearly two-decade-long ordeal for Rahim and his family.

stories.headline: Blow-by-blow account of Rahul Gandhi and CBSE's faceoff over ‘massive tampering' claim
stories.summary: Rahul Gandhi alleged "massive tampering" with the Central Board of Secondary Education's (CBSE) On-Screen Marking (OSM) system for assessing Class 12 board exam papers. The CBSE denied the claims, with the Education Minister stating that Gandhi is frustrated due to repeated election losses. Gandhi asserted that the CBSE did not address enquiries concerning purported irregularities in the evaluation. The allegations surfaced as students took to social media to report irregularities and seek justice. The CBSE stated that it had floated a tender for digital evaluation of answer books on August 28, 2025, and awarded the contract, dismissing claims of tampering. The exchange of claims and counterclaims between Gandhi and the CBSE has sparked a controversy, with the board maintaining that its evaluation process is transparent and fair.

stories.headline: India’s external shock is an economic opportunity India’s economy, despite strong fundamentals, faces external vulnerabilities from energy disruptions, shipping risks and geopolitics, requiring greater resilien
stories.summary: India's economy faces external vulnerabilities due to energy disruptions, shipping risks, and geopolitics, despite having strong fundamentals. The country is heavily reliant on crude oil imports, with prices breaching $120 per barrel in April 2026, posing risks to macroeconomic stability. The Indian crude basket's price is tied to global benchmarks, making it susceptible to supply disruptions and price volatility. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has highlighted the challenges posed by external factors and assured that the government is taking calibrated policy actions to support businesses and maintain growth momentum. High-frequency indicators such as GST collections and sales of vehicles and tractors show positive trends, indicating domestic economic activity's resilience. The government is exploring diversification, naval escorts, and a green energy transition to build long-term resilience against external shocks.

stories.headline: UK and allies have narrowing window to stay ahead in tech race, spy chief says The world is in a 'new era of radical uncertainty, contested geopolitics and rapidly changing technology,' GCHQ Director Anne Keast-Butler says
stories.summary: GCHQ Director Anne Keast-Butler warns that the UK and its allies have a narrowing window to stay ahead in the tech race. The world is in a "new era of radical uncertainty, contested geopolitics and rapidly changing technology," she says. Keast-Butler emphasizes the need to step up cyber security, making it "ten times more urgent" due to "increasingly brazen behaviour" from adversaries. Russia is a key cause of uncertainty, relentlessly targeting critical infrastructure, democratic processes, supply chains, and public trust. The UK must act quickly to maintain its advantage, as the window for doing so is rapidly closing. Keast-Butler's comments come as she delivers the first annual lecture for GCHQ, highlighting the urgent need for increased cyber security measures to protect the UK and its interests.

stories.summary: President Tinubu is set to receive the APC Certificate of Return on Sunday. Meanwhile, Ireti Kingibe has emerged as the ADC FCT Senate candidate for the 2027 elections. In other news, the Nigerian Navy, celebrating its 70th anniversary, has held a special outreach for widows across security agencies and host communities through NNS DELTA. This outreach aims to support and engage with the families of personnel and the local community. The Nigerian Navy's anniversary celebrations highlight its commitment to national security and community development. These events are part of the ongoing political and social developments in Nigeria, with various parties and institutions making preparations for future elections and engaging in community outreach programs.

stories.headline: Indian Markets Closed For Bakri Id
stories.summary: Indian stock markets, including the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), were closed on Thursday, May 28, in observance of Bakri Id, also known as Eid-al-Adha. The closure was part of the scheduled holiday list for 2026, which includes seven more market closures throughout the year for holidays such as Muharram, Ganesh Chaturthi, and Diwali. The NSE had issued an official holiday schedule, confirming the market shutdown on May 28. As a result, trading activities were halted for the day, with the markets set to resume operations on the next scheduled trading day. The closure affected both the NSE and BSE, with commodity exchanges like MCX and NCDEX also adjusting their trading timings accordingly.

stories.headline: Stock market holiday today: Are NSE, BSE open or closed on Bakri Id?
stories.summary: Indian stock markets, including the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), are closed today, May 28, 2026, on account of Bakri Id. This is the second market holiday in May, following Maharashtra Day on May 1. The closure affects morning trading in commodities, which will remain shut from 9 am to 5 pm, while the evening session will reopen from 5 pm. Trading will resume in the next regular session. The Bakri Id holiday is one of several stock market holidays scheduled for 2026, with the next trading holiday falling on June 26 for Muharram. Investors can check the complete 2026 stock market holiday calendar for upcoming closures. The MCX and NCDEX will also be affected, with settlement details and trading timings available for reference.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty outlook As per stock exchanges, trading will remain shut across equity and equity derivatives, currency derivatives, commodity derivatives and electronic gold receipts
stories.summary: Indian stock markets will be closed due to a trading holiday. The short-term market outlook is positive, with a potential uptrend rally if the Nifty breaks out above 76,200, targeting 76,800-77,000. The NIFTY BANK ended lower, down 200.75 points to 55,092.90, due to selling pressure in private lenders. Meanwhile, crude oil prices have reached a two-week high, which may lead to a muted start for the BSE Sensex and Nifty50. Precious metals, including gold and silver, are trading lower due to a strong dollar, oil price surge, and concerns over a potential Fed rate hike. The market is awaiting fresh cues to determine its next direction, with traders eyeing key levels and economic indicators for guidance. Trading is expected to resume after the holiday, with investors watching for potential breakout levels and market trends.

stories.headline: Indian stock markets remain closed today on account of Bakri Id
stories.summary: Indian stock markets are closed on May 28 for Bakri Id, with both the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) suspending trading across major segments. The closure affects most trading segments, but commodity derivatives on the Multi Commodity Exchange (MCX) will reopen for the evening session. The National Commodity & Derivatives Exchange (NCDEX) will remain shut for the day. Regular trading will resume on May 29. The next stock market holiday is scheduled for June 26, to observe Muharram. Investors are advised to check the holiday schedule to plan their trading activities accordingly. The NSE and BSE will operate as usual on May 27, prior to the Bakri Id holiday.

stories.headline: Natural News] Sam Altman’s AI job apocalypse REVERSAL looks like a calculated pivot as people fight for their livelihoods
stories.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has reversed his previous warnings about artificial intelligence eliminating entry-level white-collar jobs, stating he is "delighted to be wrong." This shift comes ahead of OpenAI's anticipated $1 trillion IPO filing. Altman cited employment data and the high costs of adopting AI technology as reasons for his revised stance. However, studies suggest AI is already impacting workers through reduced junior staff hiring and ongoing layoffs. The timing of Altman's reversal has raised questions about his motives, with some speculating it may be a calculated move to ease concerns ahead of the IPO. Despite the reversal, the impact of AI on the job market remains a concern, with many workers facing uncertainty about their livelihoods. Altman's change in stance has sparked debate about the true effects of AI on employment.

stories.headline: [The Economic Times] AI chiefs walk back job apocalypse warnings
stories.summary: Leading AI figures, including Nvidia's Jensen Huang and OpenAI's Sam Altman, are downplaying fears of mass job losses due to artificial intelligence. Huang stated that recent layoffs are not AI-driven and that earlier doomsday predictions were exaggerated. He criticized fellow executives who blame AI for workforce reductions, calling it "lazy." Both Huang and Altman had previously warned of significant job displacement due to AI, but are now walking back those comments. Nvidia has benefited greatly from the AI boom, with data center revenue growing 427% year-over-year in fiscal 2025. The shift in tone comes as OpenAI and Anthropic prepare for IPOs, each with an estimated valuation of $1 trillion. The AI chiefs' revised stance suggests they aim to mitigate backlash against the AI ecosystem, which they believe is not solely responsible for job losses.

stories.headline: [ScienceAlert] Stunning AI Solution For 80-Year-Old Problem Shocks Mathematicians
stories.summary: OpenAI's internal AI model has solved a famous math conjecture that had puzzled humans for nearly 80 years. The breakthrough is being hailed as a "seismic shift" in the way mathematics is discovered. The conjecture, which had gone unsolved for eight decades, was recently cracked by the AI model, shocking mathematicians. This achievement demonstrates the potential of artificial intelligence in advancing mathematical knowledge. The solution is considered a significant milestone, showcasing the capabilities of AI in solving complex problems that have stumped human mathematicians for years. The development has sparked interest and debate about the role of AI in mathematical discovery and its potential to accelerate progress in the field.

stories.headline: [Markets Insider] Anthropic’s Revenue Surpasses OpenAI as Companies Race Toward IPOs
stories.summary: Anthropic's revenue has surpassed that of OpenAI, with an estimated 35% more revenue. Anthropic's annualized revenue reached $45 billion, compared to OpenAI's $33 billion. This shift comes as both companies prepare for initial public offerings (IPOs) later this year. Anthropic reported its first quarterly operating profit of $559 million, signaling a major shift in the AI market. The company's expansion into business-focused applications has driven its growth, with over 1,000 enterprise customers spending over $1 million annually. Anthropic achieved $30 billion in annual recurring revenue (ARR) in April 2026, overtaking OpenAI for the first time, and is now targeting an IPO for October. The company has experienced 30x growth in 15 months, intensifying global competition among leading AI companies.
